analysis: Changes examined: (1) ProviderLoop+InferenceHandler.swift replaces autopilotAllowsModel with autopilotServesModel at two admission points (throwIfRefusingNewLocalWork, line ~135, and the authoritative pre-registration autopilot check, line ~513). The visible head text (lines 620-1556) is unchanged context: the response-encryption fail-closed path (precomputeSharedKey and emitSSE failures send an encryptionFailure terminal, no plaintext fallback, T-008), cancellation, receipt finalization, cache-scope plumbing (remoteCache.scope, T-041) and the billing floor. None of these were modified. The definition of autopilotServesModel is not supplied. If it is looser than autopilotAllowsModel, it could admit network work for models autopilot had not selected. I cannot verify this from the supplied evidence, so I report no finding, but integration should confirm that autopilotServesModel is at least as restrictive for network-origin requests as the old predicate. (2) ProviderLoop+MTPUpgrade.swift adds transitionGenerations.begin(.modelLoading) at line 127, right after isLoadingAny = true in prepareRetainedMTPUpgrade. The matching end or completion is not visible. The defers at lines 128-129 only finish deviceActivity and clear isLoadingAny. If begin requires a paired end, the early-throw paths (insufficientMemory at line 136, and the catch at 187-199) could leave a generation open. That could stall dependent logic or availability. If begin is a monotonic generation bump, it is benign. This needs checking against the transitionGenerations type, which is outside this batch. No data-exposure, encryption, attestation or billing behavior changed in the supplied lines. Remaining questions: the semantics of autopilotServesModel and of transitionGenerations.begin/.modelLoading, including whether there is an unmatched end.
